# gitlab_repository_files (Resource)

The `gitlab_repository_files` resource manages the lifecycle of a set of related files within a repository as a single atomic commit, using GitLab's multi-file commit API instead of `gitlab_repository_file`'s one-commit-per-file approach.

-> **Timeouts** Default timeout for *Create*, *Read*, *Update* and *Delete* is 10 minutes and can be configured in the `timeouts` attribute.

-> **Implementation Detail** This resource shares its internal call queue with `gitlab_repository_file`, since GitLab cannot handle concurrent calls to the repository files/commits API for the same project no matter which resource issues them.

-> Files in `file` that already exist on the branch are adopted instead of failing the create: a file whose content and execute flag already match is left out of the commit, and when every file matches no commit is made and `commit_id` stays unset. Adopted files are deleted on destroy like any other file this resource manages.

-> Import (`project:branch`) records only the project and branch. The next apply adopts the files listed in `file` the same way create does, so the first plan after import always shows an update even when the branch already matches.

-> Changing a file's `file_path` is committed as a move of the file to the new path, as long as its bytes and execute flag are unchanged (switching `encoding` alone does not change the bytes); anything else changing alongside the path is a delete of the old path and a create of the new one. A move is only inferred when exactly one old path matches exactly one new path by content; ambiguous matches fall back to a delete and a create. A path that already exists on the branch is never the target of a move.

**Upstream API**: [GitLab REST API docs](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/commits/#create-a-commit-with-multiple-files-and-actions)

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "gitlab_group" "this" {
  name        = "example"
  path        = "example"
  description = "An example group"
}
resource "gitlab_project" "this" {
  name                   = "example"
  namespace_id           = gitlab_group.this.id
  initialize_with_readme = true
}

resource "gitlab_repository_files" "this" {
  project = gitlab_project.this.id
  branch  = "main"

  create_commit_message = "Scaffold example project"
  update_commit_message = "Update example project scaffold"
  delete_commit_message = "Remove example project scaffold"

  file = [
    {
      file_path = "main.tf"
      content   = "# placeholder"
    },
    {
      file_path = "provider.tf"
      content   = "# placeholder"
    },
    {
      file_path = "variables.tf"
      content   = "# placeholder"
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `branch` (String) Name of the branch to which to commit to.
- `file` (Attributes Set) One object per file managed as part of this atomic commit set. Adding, removing, or editing an object adds, removes, or updates that one file in the next commit this resource makes - unchanged files are left out of that commit entirely. Between 1 and 100 objects are allowed, and each `file_path` may appear only once. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--file))
- `project` (String) The name or ID of the project.

### Optional

- `author_email` (String) Email of the commit author.
- `author_name` (String) Name of the commit author.
- `commit_message` (String) Commit message used for whichever operation (create, update, delete) is being performed. Either this or `create_commit_message`, `update_commit_message`, and `delete_commit_message` must be set.
- `create_commit_message` (String) Create commit message.
- `delete_commit_message` (String) Delete commit message.
- `start_branch` (String) Name of the branch to start the new commit from. Only used on create, and `branch` must not exist yet.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `update_commit_message` (String) Update commit message.

### Read-Only

- `commit_id` (String) The commit id of the most recent commit made by this resource. Unset until this resource makes a commit.
- `id` (String) The ID of this Terraform resource. In the format of `<project>:<branch>`.

<a id="nestedatt--file"></a>
### Nested Schema for `file`

Required:

- `content` (String) File content.
- `file_path` (String) The full path of the file. It must be relative to the root of the project without a leading slash `/` or `./`.

Optional:

- `encoding` (String) The file content encoding. Valid values are: `base64`, `text`. Defaults to `text`.
- `execute_filemode` (Boolean) Enables or disables the execute flag on the file. Defaults to `false`.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Starting in Terraform v1.5.0, you can use an [import block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import `gitlab_repository_files`. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = gitlab_repository_files.example
  id = "see CLI command below for ID"
}
```

Importing using the CLI is supported with the following syntax:

```shell
# A gitlab_repository_files resource can be imported using an id made up of `<project>:<branch-name>`, for example:
terraform import gitlab_repository_files.this 1:main
# Where `project` may be the project ID or path with namespace depending on what you have in your config.
# Import records only the project and branch. The next apply adopts the files listed in `file`,
# committing only those that differ from the branch.
```
